text:
zara-sales: FYI customer POC is hitting a burst of 5xxs during a ramp. Need quick triage and mitigation checklist. Customer is on Dedicated trial.
joe-support: Thanks. Which errors specifically? 503 or 504? Any request IDs we can grep?
maya-se: Seeing a pattern: 503 capacity_throttled in the runtime logs, autoscaler lagged ~2m during the ramp. Customer traffic spiked from 10rps -> 140rps in 90s.
chris-eng: Can we get the swarm/worker side logs and the autoscaler events? If autoscaler missed the window, we might need temporary burstpool config or manual scale.
alex-customer: attaching sample from our side (sanitized):
```
2026-03-19T14:22:01Z ERROR request_id=abc123 rh=5xx capacity_throttled model=redwood-7b kv_cache_hit=0
2026-03-19T14:22:02Z WARN request_id=abc124 queue_ms=1200 backend_queued=true
503 Service Unavailable
```
joe-support: Ok. First quick mitigation options to propose to customer:
- enable model fallback to a smaller compatible variant (e.g., rwd-7b -> rwd-3b) for burst periods
- temporarily increase reserved capacity / add burstpool if on Dedicated
- enable prefix caching for repeated prompts
- shorten max_tokens and reduce concurrency from client side
maya-se: Also toggle autoscaler aggressiveness: lower scale_up_cooldown to 30s and reduce threshold from 70%->60% for this POC window.
chris-eng: For fast triage, run these checks:
1) confirm autoscaler events:
   kubectl -n redwood get hpa|jq .  # or check our custom scaler logs
2) search runtime logs for "capacity_throttled" and request IDs
   rg "capacity_throttled" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 100
3) check queue depth & token backlog in console /api/metrics
joe-support: If customer prefers a config change we can do a temporary canary deploy to increase pool size. We should also prepare rollback steps.
zara-sales: Customer asked about cost impact of increasing burstpool for a few hours — can we run an estimate?
maya-se: Quick rule of thumb: hourly GPU cost * number_of_gpus * hours. I'll ping infra-costs channel and get exact estimate.
deploy-bot: notice: autoscaler_scale_event id=scale-789 created=2026-03-19T14:23:30Z from 4->8 pods reason=cpu_queue_spike
chris-eng: Noted the scale event — but laged 90s after the traffic ramp. That explains 5xx burst. Root causes to record:
- aggressive client ramp without gradual ramp-up
- autoscaler cooldown and threshold tuned for steady state, not spikes
- no temporary fallback model configured
joe-support: Action items for this thread (quick):
- @maya-se prepare config patch for lower cooldown + fallback policy (SE runbook)
- @chris-eng prepare a one-off burstpool increase playbook + rollback
- @zara-sales give customer the mitigation checklist and cost estimate
- @alex-customer apply client-side throttling to smooth ramp (100rps max, +10rps/sec)
zara-sales: I'll share checklist and ask for a 3hr maintenance window to test fixes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
maya-se: I'll also add a snippet they can paste to enable fallback in their config:
```
routing:
  fallback_variant: rwd-3b
  fallback_threshold: 0.75
autoscaler:
  scale_up_cooldown: 30s
  cpu_threshold: 60
```
joe-support: I'll open a support ticket with case_id=SUP-2026-903 and attach logs + timeline.
alex-customer: Thanks team — applying client-side smoothing now. Will report back in ~15m.
chris-eng: If we see remaining 5xx after mitigations, escalate to infra and we may need an emergency hotfix to scheduler.
maya-se: Good plan. Keeping this thread for updates.
